description: Progressive bearing damage or lubrication-related distress.
Vapor bubble formation/collapse due to inadequate suction conditions.
Pump and motor shaft centerlines are not correctly aligned.
Deposits or foreign material restrict impeller passages.
Seal faces or elastomers are worn, damaged, or thermally distressed.
Restriction on suction side reduces available flow and inlet pressure.
Pump operates with insufficient liquid, causing loss of cooling/lubrication.
Driver current/power exceeds expected operating condition.
Flexible element wear, looseness, or coupling damage.
Impeller surfaces are eroded, cracked, or otherwise mechanically damaged.
Excessive discharge-side restriction moves pump toward low-flow operation.
Air enters suction piping or fittings and disrupts hydraulic performance.
Loose hold-down bolts, soft foot, or weak foundation increases vibration.
Voltage/current phase imbalance causes motor heating and unstable operation.
